title: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Seventh edition, Volume 13, LAB-Magnetism - EB.15
text: _Linn in the Celtic or ancient British language signified a lake, and for an town or a harbour in ships. A small recent dates the Surrey side of the river was often a lake in some parts, and a swamp in others, the name might be easily changed the Linden in London, and be descriptive of its local position. It could not, however, No a place of very great importance at the time of the invasion of Engeland by Julian Essas; for thought that comments must have passed near it, he has now noticed it in his Comentertains.
